summary: Discovery for Dedicated GPU capacity for Riverfront Bank. Main concerns: data isolation / VPC, burst strategy for peak trading hours, predictable latency and cost, KMS integration and SOC2 compliance. Customer leaning toward Dedicated with private control plane but wants pilot + benchmarks.
transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Anna Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Torres (Redwood SE), Lisa Monroe (CTO, Riverfront), Raj Kapoor (Head of ML), Tom Ellis (Security Lead), Maya Singh (Platform).
Links referenced: Redwood Dedicated one-pager, benchmark spreadsheet (shared), SOC2 whitepaper (link).
[00:00] Anna Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Anna from Redwood, this is Miguel on the SE side. um quick intro then we can jump into your current stack and goals.
[00:15] Lisa Monroe: Hi all, Lisa here. thanks. We're interested in understanding dedicated capacity options, mostly around reserved gpus, isolation and burst.
[00:30] Raj Kapoor: Yeah our main driver is consistent latency for prod features - customer-facing assistants and document search - and we need to control cost.
[00:45] Miguel Torres: Great, so just to set expectations, Dedicated means you get a reserved pool of GPU instances, predictable throughput, option for a private control plane and VPC peering. we do autoscale within the pool and we offer burst credits for short spikes.
[01:10] Tom Ellis: Quick security q - does Dedicated keep data in our VPC? encryption at rest w/ KMS? audit logs?
[01:25] Miguel Torres: Yes, you can choose Private deployment which gives you customer-managed VPC and optional on-prem package. We integrate with customer KMS/HSM for at-rest keys, and audit logs are available through the console and can be pushed to your SIEM.
[01:45] Maya Singh: For the burst story - are bursts additional machines outside our reserved pool, or do you have a credit system? how does billing work for bursts vs reserved?
[02:05] Anna Chen: Good q. reserved capacity is committed monthly/annual. Burst is allowed as configurable burst capacity - typically billed at a higher per-hour rate and capped. For budgeting we show estimates in the pricing deck. We'll send the detailed tiers.
[02:25] Raj Kapoor: Our workload has heavy morning spikes around 09:00-10:30 and periodic end-of-day reconciliations. Peak QPS is about 120 requests/sec for generation with avg 350 tokens per request. Sustained baseline is ~20 QPS.
[02:50] Miguel Torres: ok that's helpful. Do you have token distribution? like many short prompts or few long ones?
[03:05] Raj Kapoor: Mixed. 70% short prompts (50-200 tokens), 30% longer summaries (300-800). KV cache reuse is important - we rely on prefix caching for session-based assistants.
[03:25] Miguel Torres: Perfect - Our runtime supports KV cache pooling and prefix caching which reduces per-token cost for repeated contexts. We'll note cache hit expectations when we run benchmarks.
[03:40] Lisa Monroe: On model choice: are you hosting open models? we can't use closed cloud LLMs for some PII data.
[03:55] Miguel Torres: Redwood supports curated open models and we also provide re-verified performance profiles. For Dedicated you can pin model versions and we can host open quantized variants if you want.
[04:10] Tom Ellis: SOC2? Any ISO certs? we need proof for procurement. Also SSO/SAML + RBAC.
[04:25] Anna Chen: We are SOC2 compliant - I'll attach the SOC2 whitepaper and security FAQ. SSO/SAML and RBAC are supported; for Private deployments you can integrate with your IdP and enforce RBAC.
[04:40] Maya Singh: Network egress - do you route traffic through Redwood control plane or is it direct? concerns about data egress/residency.
[04:55] Miguel Torres: With Private you keep control plane in your VPC, data stays in your region. For hosted Dedicated we'll provide options for region pinning and private peering. We'll outline egress patterns in the architecture doc.
[05:15] Lisa Monroe: Pricing sensitivity - we have a finance review. we need predictable unit economics, per-token costs and also a way to simulate monthly spend under different traffic patterns.
[05:30] Anna Chen: We'll provide a costing model and an example calc for your traffic profile. plus reserved vs burst vs on-demand comparisons.
[05:40] Raj Kapoor: For pilot we want to run a small reserved pool - maybe 2-4 GPUs - and then run our prompt sets to compare latency and throughput against our on-prem baseline and Anthropic/other vendors.
[05:55] Miguel Torres: That aligns with our typical pilot. We recommend starting with a small dedicated pool sized for baseline with burst enabled for peak windows. We can run joint benchmarks: we provide scripts and configs, you run your prompt set, we return token-level latency and cost breakdowns.
[06:15] Lisa Monroe: SLA - we need 99.9% availability and an escalation path.
[06:25] Anna Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA options; for enterprise we offer higher uptime commitments and a named escalation contact. We'll include SLA details in the proposal.
[06:35] Tom Ellis: A couple specifics on KMS - does Redwood support customer-managed keys in AWS KMS and GCP KMS? key rotation policy?
[06:50] Miguel Torres: yes we support AWS KMS and GCP KMS for Private; HSM integrations for on-prem. Rotation policies are yours to manage; Redwood will not have plaintext access to the keys.
[07:05] Raj Kapoor: When you say autoscale within the pool, what's the granularity? how fast can you add capacity?
[07:20] Miguel Torres: autoscale within reserved pool is seat-based; scaling is near-instant within pre-provisioned capacity. for adding more reserved GPUs (upscaling the pool size) that's a provisioning operation that typically takes hours depending on region and inventory, so for predictable growth we recommend planning a capacity window. for sudden spikes we rely on burst.
[07:45] Maya Singh: Do you support model quantization variants to reduce GPU memory and increase concurrency?
[07:55] Miguel Torres: Absolutely - Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles per workload. We can serve quantized variants which improves density and lowers cost, with a minor quality tradeoff we can quantify in evals.
[08:10] Lisa Monroe: Any gotchas with Kubernetes or our infra team needing to manage nodes?
[08:20] Miguel Torres: For Private you can run the on-prem package which is k8s-friendly; we provide helm charts and operator. For Dedicated managed by Redwood you won't need to orchestrate nodes.
[08:35] Raj Kapoor: Benchmark question - can we test real-time latency at 99th percentile for 300-token responses? that's our main SLO.
[08:50] Miguel Torres: yes we'll capture P50/P95/P99 for token-level and request-level latency. We'll also include cold-start characteristics and KV cache warmup effects.
[09:05] Tom Ellis: Data deletion policies? retention windows? we need to ensure transcripts aren't retained by vendor.
[09:20] Anna Chen: You can configure data retention policies; for Private deployments you can opt-out of logging/raw transcript persistence. We'll document default retention and how to disable.
[09:35] Lisa Monroe: Are there examples of other financial customers using Dedicated? any references?
[09:45] Anna Chen: We can share anonymized case studies; I'll include one-pager and a reference contact where allowed.
[09:55] Raj Kapoor: Integration - we need a test env that mirrors prod networking. is staging in our VPC possible?
[10:10] Miguel Torres: yes for Private or VPC-backed Dedicated we can provision a staging pool in your VPC. That is how customers validate network rules.
[10:25] Maya Singh: on telemetry - do you expose per-route latency and token counts in the console? we want to hook into our observability.
[10:35] Miguel Torres: yes console has per-route token counts, latency histograms, trace ids. We also provide trace hooks and can stream metrics to your monitoring stack.
[10:50] Anna Chen: quick recap and next steps: We'll send pricing + SOC2 + benchmark kit. Miguel will share benchmark spreadsheet and configs. Raj to provide prompts and traffic profile. We'll target pilot kickoff week of 3/16.
[11:10] Lisa Monroe: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[11:20] (call ends)
Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings e.g., "KV cache" noted as "K V cache" in places; speaker tags sometimes generic.
